summary: Silver Lake Capital is evaluating Redwood for LLM inference across hosted/dedicated/private modes. Primary concerns: EU/US data residency, log retention and redaction, HIPAA-ish controls for certain funds, KMS/HSM key control, audit logs, and network isolation in VPC/on-prem. AE + SE discussed tradeoffs, proposed next steps for a private deployment diagram and SOC2 docs, and tentatively scoped Dedicated reserved capacity for an 8-GPU pilot.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-18
Time: 15:00 EDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Solutions), Tom (Silver Lake Head of Cloud), Anita (CISO), Ethan (Compliance), Liam (DevOps)
Shared artifacts: redwood_security_whitepaper_v2.pdf (link), private-deploy-diagram.png (to be shared), pricing-estimate-template.xlsx (mentioned)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Tom: hi tom bennett here, head of cloud platform at silver lake, we run a hybrid multi-cloud footprint, lots of EU customers, and finance regs.
[00:15] Anita: anita, ciso, i'll be focusing on controls, encryption, and auditability.
[00:20] Diego: diego, se at redwood, i'll cover architecture and ops details.
[00:28] Priya: priya on solutions, i'll help with onboarding questions.
[00:33] Anita: quick note - some of the funds we manage are subject to GDPR and also some HIPAA-like constraints for health-related portcos, so we need clarity on data flows.
[00:45] Maya: totally. goal for today is to surface residency requirements, logging/retention needs, and to map which deployment mode makes sense — hosted, dedicated, or private.
[00:55] Ethan: timeline is roughly q3 pilot then enterprise roll by q4 if controls check out. key success criteria: no cross-border movement of PII in the EU use cases, ability to restrict logs with PII redaction, and bring-your-own-key for encryption.
[01:15] Diego: on the technical side, redwood hosted has regions in eu-west and us-east. for many customers EU-only data residency is satisfied by routing requests to eu regions and disabling cross-region backups; but we do have constraints around logs and retained artifacts.
[01:35] Anita: when you say logs, do you mean request/response text logs? our legal team will not accept raw prompts being stored outside customer control.
[01:45] Diego: right, so hosted by default keeps minimal telemetry, but for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool in our cloud region — data stays in that region and we can configure limited logging. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you the most control: private control plane, customer-managed network, and you can use your KMS/HSM.
[02:10] Liam: can you say more about KMS integration? we use AWS KMS with CloudHSM and need key ownership.
[02:18] Diego: with Private we support BYOK head-node integration and HSM-backed keys. we can do envelope encryption so the model artifacts and request payloads are encrypted with keys you manage. on Dedicated we have an option to integrate with your KMS for disk and s3-level encryption but we still manage the control plane — that may not satisfy strict customer-managed key policies.
[02:42] Tom: latency/cost concerns — we have high throughput inference for scoring pipelines and we can't tolerate a big latency uplift for the eu scoring path. how different is Dedicated vs Private in perf?
[02:55] Diego: performance-wise the runtime is the same; Dedicated uses our managed cluster in your chosen region so you get comparable latency to hosted. Private on-prem will depend on your infra, but our guidance is that for low-latency you colocate GPUs in the same region/az as callers. additional network hops for private control plane can be minimized with a local control plane option.
[03:20] Anita: audit logs are critical. we need tamper-evident logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and exportable logs for audits. are those available?
[03:30] Maya: yes, we provide audit logs, SAML SSO integrations, and fine-grained RBAC. for Private deployments you get full control and can ship logs to your SIEM (Splunk/ELK). for Hosted we offer audit logs but retention/export policies are configurable only within our tenancy — we'll share details in the SOC2 docs.
[03:55] Ethan: question on PII in logs — can you redact tokens or obfuscate responses at ingestion?
[04:03] Diego: we offer configurable log redaction and prefix-filtering. for highest assurance customers we recommend request proxying and client-side redaction before sending. also we support disabling request/response logging entirely in Private. note: disabling logs affects troubleshooting and observability.
[04:30] Anita: about HIPAA controls — do you sign a BAA and support HIPAA workload patterns?
[04:37] Maya: we have customers with HIPAA needs; we can discuss BAA — it depends on deployment and the contract. Private deployments usually are the path for PHI because you can ensure network isolation and key control.
[04:52] Tom: any constraints around model artifacts? we want to ensure models trained/fine-tuned on our data don't leave our environment.
[04:59] Diego: by default models offered in hosted are shared; for dedicated you can bring your own model or we can provision a private model repo tied to your tenancy. Private lets you run models entirely inside your VPC/on-prem so artifacts never leave. we'll need to discuss license constraints.
[05:20] Liam: what about backup/replication? replication to a DR region in the US is a no-go for EU-only data.
[05:27] Diego: we can configure replication boundaries and disable cross-region DR for Dedicated/Private. for hosted it may be trickier; we'll need legal sign-off.
[05:40] Tom: onboarding effort — how long for a Dedicated pilot?
[05:46] Priya: typical Dedicated pilot with reserved pool and onboarding takes 3-4 weeks: provisioning, network peering, KMS integration, and a test workload. Private deployments are longer — depending on on-prem capacity and security review, usually 6-8 weeks.
[06:05] Anita: auditability during the pilot — can we get a test harness to validate logs and retention?
[06:11] Diego: yes we'll provide a test harness and sample eval prompts, plus a checklist for controls to validate.
[06:20] Ethan: data retention policy for logs — what default retention do you have and can we set strict limits?
[06:27] Maya: default telemetry is 90 days for hosted, but enterprise customers can configure retention, and Private gives full control to export/retain via your SIEM. we'll list specifics in the SOC2 packet.
[06:40] Tom: what about access controls to model logs — can we restrict who at redwood sees raw requests?
[06:47] Diego: access is strictly role-based; for Dedicated we can set service accounts with least privilege and for Private we can configure no access to redwood engineers by default (support access requires explicit allow).
[07:03] Anita: any known compliance certifications beyond SOC2?
[07:08] Maya: SOC2 is standard, we also pursue ISO27001; some customers ask for FedRAMP — we're evaluating roadmap. we'll include current certification PDFs in follow-up.
[07:21] Ethan: ok on encryption in transit; what about encryption of KV cache and ephemeral tensors?
[07:29] Diego: runtime encrypts KV cache at rest; in-memory is protected by host isolation. for customers with very high security needs, Private with dedicated hardware and encrypted swap can be arranged.
[07:45] Liam: RTO/RPO questions — for Dedicated pilot with 8 GPUs, what does outage look like and do you offer fallback to hosted?
[07:54] Diego: yes we can set fallback policy to route requests to a compatible hosted model variant if Dedicated capacity is fully degraded — that's part of our graceful degradation story. TTLs and fallbacks are configurable per-route.
[08:10] Tom: pricing — can you provide a ballpark for an 8 GPU committed Dedicated cluster?
[08:15] Maya: we'll share a pricing estimate. rough ballpark in the doc we send; final numbers depend on GPU type and committed term.
[08:25] Anita: legal/procurement — we expect redline on DPA and security addendum; will you accept our standard DPA?
[08:33] Maya: we'll review and typically we can align on enterprise DPAs; some items around data egress and KMS need special attention.
[08:45] Ethan: competitors — we've spoken to BigCloudAI; they claim region-locking but their key management is limited. how do you compare?
[08:55] Diego: we offer BYOK on Private and stronger logging controls; we'll include a short comparison in follow-up.
[09:05] Tom: sounds good. next steps recap?
[09:09] Maya: we'll send: SOC2 + ISO docs, private deployment diagram, Dedicated pilot pricing, and schedule deep dive week of 4/27.
[09:18] Anita: i'll share a redacted list of regulated dataflows and our DPA template.
[09:22] Maya: action items noted. thanks all.
[09:28] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker label mismatches and filler words preserved. There are small transcription artifacts: 'HSM' spelled 'H-S-M', 'KV cache' as 'K V cache' in places.
